fundamentals.ponder.mixer_settler.header: Parting the rare earths in a mixer-settler battery
fundamentals.ponder.mixer_settler.text_1: Casings placed facing the same way merge into one vat: three across, three along, one or two tall. Nine casings are a lab vat, eighteen a plant vat.
fundamentals.ponder.mixer_settler.text_2: The back row is the mixing box. A Mechanical Mixer standing over its hatch, driven by a cogwheel beside it, beats the two liquids together; the rows ahead are the settling bay, where they part again.
fundamentals.ponder.mixer_settler.text_3: Charge the extractant, P507 here, through the top. It floats on the liquor and is never used up: it only ferries the heavier rare earths forward, stage by stage.
fundamentals.ponder.mixer_settler.text_4: The liquor goes in at the back of the first stage and the strip acid at the front of the last. The raffinate leaves the first stage by its sides, the loaded strip the last stage by its sides.
fundamentals.ponder.mixer_settler.text_5: A lever on the head stage starts the battery. Stages standing end to end are one battery, and each cut needs a set number: eight to part the lights from the heavies, thirty-two to part neodymium from praseodymium.
fundamentals.ponder.mixer_settler.text_6: Every cut leaves a fifth of a batch of spent liquor in a sump under the head stage. Pump it out from below and neutralise it with lime, or the battery stops when the sump is full.
fundamentals.ponder.mixer_settler.text_7: Goggles on any casing tell you what the battery holds, what it is waiting for, and how far the organic and the liquor have got down the line.
